name: Patriarchate of Aquileia
alt: Temporal state of the Patriarchs of Aquileia

predecessors.name: March of Verona
predecessors.text: the Friulian lands, a Carolingian march from 828 reorganised into the March of Friuli, added to the March of Verona in 952, in which Henry IV vested Patriarch Sieghard with 'immediate comital rights'…

successors.name: Republic of Venice
successors.text: Friuli, 'Venetians thus annexed the territory, depriving the Patriarch of Aquileia of his temporal powers'; Cliopatria's Venice shape of 1422 holds 26 of the 32 cells of the Patriarchate's 1407 shape

ledger.x: 1077: Henry IV makes the Patriarch of Aquileia count of Friuli.
1209: the patriarchs regain the Istrian march.
1291: Venice keeps the western Istrian coast.
1420: Muggia, Labin and Plomin surrender to Venice.
1420: Gemona, San Daniele, Venzone and Tolmezzo fall.
1420: the Venetian war ends with the end of the patriarchs' temporal power.
1420: the Patriarchal State of Friuli is annexed by Venice.

wars.name: War of the Patriarchal State of Friuli, 1411-1420
wars.outcome: A civil war between Cividale and Udine in 1411 (Udine captured by an Imperial army in December 1411) became a Venetian conquest: Cividale fell on 23 July 1419, Udine on 7 June 1420 and the patriarch's temporal power ended on 7 July 1420.

certainty.note: No page opened gives a boundary of the Patria del Friuli; the outlines are Cliopatria's approximations and the Istrian edge is the softest.
